cerebras_503_reconciliation.claim_under_investigation: A real Cerebras 503 was observed ONCE during the Phase-9 Step 6/7 baseline run and reportedly 'absorbed transparently' with no user-visible failure - does this contradict candidate_b_native_tools.py's documented 'zero retry' design?
evidence_examined: artifacts/v2/phase9_baseline_results.json - the 12 baseline case error fields contain NO Cerebras-shaped error string (candidate_b_native_tools.py's own error format is exactly f'HTTP {status}: {text}'); none of the 12 cases' errors match that shape at status 503.

logs/medagent.log lines 3423-3819+ (session 2026-09-25T00:41:43Z-00:46:17Z) show every 503 occurrence in that session logged by logger='config.llm_config' with message text '[LLM DISPATCH RESULT] ... error=Exception: [###] {\'message\': \'Service temporarily overloaded\', \'type\': \'Service Unavailable\', \'code\': 503}' followed by '[LLM RETRY] Call failed with a retryable provider error (attempt N/3): ... discarding client and retrying with a fresh connection'.

The '[###] {...}' message shape is langchain_nvidia_ai_endpoints' own internal error-string format (documented in config/llm_config.py's _RETRYABLE_ERROR_MARKERS comment: '_common.py's _try_raise ... e.g. "[###] {...code: 503...}"'), NOT orchestration/candidate_b_native_tools.py's format.
No log line in the entire session log matches candidate_b_native_tools.py's own error string format with a 503 status anywhere.

conclusion.exact_call_that_got_the_503: An NVIDIA NIM ChatNVIDIA.invoke() call (query-analysis/synthesis/report/judge - whichever node's get_llm() call was in flight at 2026-09-25T00:41:43Z), NOT a call_cerebras_native_tools() tool-selection call.
conclusion.exact_function_class_handling_it: config/llm_config.py::_RateLimitedChatNVIDIA.invoke() - its _is_retryable_llm_error() substring match on '503'/'Service Unavailable' classified it retryable, then it discarded the client, constructed a fresh ChatNVIDIA, slept a calculated backoff, and retried (up to LLM_CALL_MAX_ATTEMPTS=3 total attempts).
conclusion.tool_selection_or_other_path: Other path - this is implementation #1 (NVIDIA NIM client), not implementation #2 (Cerebras tool-selection, candidate_b_native_tools.py).
conclusion.mechanism: config.llm_config._RateLimitedChatNVIDIA's own bounded retry-with-fresh-client logic (LLM_CALL_MAX_ATTEMPTS=3), not a LangGraph-level or node-level fallback.
conclusion.verdict_text: 'Zero retry' remains an ACCURATE characterization of call_cerebras_native_tools() specifically. The one real 503 'absorbed transparently' during the Phase-9 baseline run was on a DIFFERENT provider-call implementation (NVIDIA NIM via ChatNVIDIA, implementation #1), which was always designed to retry 429/503-classified errors (see PHASE9_INITIAL_AUDIT.md Section 3, item 1) - this was that mechanism working exactly as documented, not a contradiction of the Cerebras tool-selection path's deliberate zero-retry design (implementation #2). The initial framing in the governing directive's context note ('A real Cerebras 503 was observed') is a mischaracterization of provider attribution, corrected here by direct log evidence; the underlying reliability behavior (a transient 503 being absorbed without a user-visible failure) is real and correctly attributed to implementation #1's retry policy, not implementation #2's absence of one.
